baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Uses Elizabeth Marsh’s itinerant life to investigate transcontinental connections and women’s place in global history.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Author’s answers on biography, missing letters and reconstructing Marsh through others’ writings. This identifies a specific biographical project, without treating one life as representative of every woman or attributing the book’s sources to Colley.

baseline_incident_edges.relationship: Colley values Bailyn’s Atlantic connections but challenges strong claims for their regional unity and the exclusion of early Asian connections.
baseline_incident_edges.evidence_note: Her 2006 review distinguishes praise for Atlantic inquiry from criticism of Bailyn’s stronger geographical model. The unity discussion at the end of section 1 and Asia discussion at the end of section 2 support this limited objection. Pestana’s book is separately reviewed; its claims are not silently assigned to Bailyn. No blanket rejection of Atlantic history or fresh reading of Bailyn’s whole 2005 book is asserted.
